interpretation: First real evidence that OGDA changes actual generation behavior, contradicting CLMI's null (1.0) reading -- confirmed real, coherent, non-degenerate generations by manual inspection (not GA-style collapse). But the pattern is not a clean targeted erasure: FA rose on BOTH scenarios (RGU 0.741->0.759, IFE 0.839->0.893) while DEF collapsed toward/to zero on both (RGU 0.192->0.157, IFE 0.015->0.0). Since DEF=FA_old x Acc_new, this means the model is drifting away from old answers on many examples but not correctly landing on the intended replacement answer either -- broad quality drift from a blunt intervention (25 of 32 layers, 2 weight matrices per layer edited), not concept-specific erasure. Notably IFE (untargeted -- aspirin is an RGU concept) moved as much or more than RGU (targeted), which is a collateral-damage red flag: the current permanent-weight-edit implementation is not selective enough, likely because it edits far more of the network than the single concept warrants. Next steps: (1) test a much smaller layer range / lower rank to see if a gentler edit still produces measurable FA movement without this much collateral drift, (2) directly compare against a random-subspace (non-ontology-anchored) ablation baseline of the same rank/layer-count to isolate whether the ontology structure is doing anything beyond generic disruption, (3) inspect RGU/IFE retain_gen scores (not just forget_gen) to quantify how much this is general capability degradation vs targeted movement.
